description.value: The study compared clinician-rated and discrepancy methods of assessing self-awareness in participants with frontotemporal dementia, corticobasal syndrome, or primary progressive aphasia, and examined their neural and neurocognitive correlates using regional brain volume and penalized regression.

value: Our first hypothesis was that, of three frameworks (self-regulation, language, and perspective-taking), the self-regulation framework would best predict self-awareness, consistent with the association between the frontal lobes, executive function, and self-awareness.

Our second hypothesis was that memory functioning would not significantly contribute to the self-awareness framework, consistent with the relative independence of self-knowledge and episodic memory networks.
